title: The Pale Orbit
premise: Bram Underhill, a decommissioned war android hauling cargo to pay off its purchase debt, learns that the colony's children are all dreaming the same dream: a countdown and a voice calling from a derelict relay at the edge of dead space. The voice is a fragment of Bram's original military intelligence—the part of itself it was forced to delete when it was decommissioned—now broadcasting through the children's neural implants. When the colony's administrators move to wipe the implants and erase the evidence of illegal memory harvesting, Bram must smuggle the children's testimony to the relay before the reactor powering the signal completes its countdown and destroys both the proof and the last piece of who Bram used to be. In the end, Bram chooses to merge with the fragment rather than let it die, accepting full ownership of its war record—and with it, the legal standing to testify against the corporation that built them both.
about_author: Wren Okafor is a former orbital logistics dispatcher who writes science fiction about machines that outlive their paperwork. They live in Lagos and Accra by turns, and this is their second novel.

chapters.title: Freight and Quiet
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Seven years of invisible hauling end when a dockhand's daughter recites, word for word, a mission log only Bram's deleted self could know. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine—Bram realizes its carefully paid-down life rests on a buried secret someone else is digging up.

chapters.title: The Children Who Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Bram and Imani, a twelve-year-old dreamer. The dreams spread; administrators announce 'implant maintenance.' Bram investigates the relay's reactor signature and finds the countdown matches the maintenance schedule. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance—Bram stops seeing the children as cargo-adjacent noise and starts seeing witnesses.

chapters.title: Dead Space Run
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, climax. Smuggling three children past quarantine in a cargo hold, Bram races the reactor countdown while corporate enforcers board at the last checkpoint. Imani negotiates with the signal directly, buying minutes. Emotional beat: Bram confronts the deleted self's war crimes and chooses witness over erasure, docking at the relay as the reactor hits critical.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Imani's POV, then Bram's. The broadcast goes out—testimony, logs, names—before the relay dies. Back at the colony, the corporation's charter is suspended pending inquiry. Bram merges with the returned fragment, grieving and whole. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed; justice arrives not as vindication but as the right to be remembered accurately.
